title: Use the data to complete the example
subtitle: Command of Evidence · 51 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **51 of the official questions in Command of Evidence are this one** — 30 Easy, 13 Medium, 8 Hard.
It is bottom-heavy, which makes it cheap points. Secure it early.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- There is a table or graph, and the passage ends with an unfinished sentence, often after 'for example' or 'the highest number...'.
- The question asks which choice most effectively uses data from the table/graph to complete the statement.
- The choices are data comparisons such as 'X was higher than Y'.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Before looking at the choices, work out what the sentence needs to demonstrate: a difference, a similarity, a maximum or a trend.
- 2) Rule out choices that misread the data.
- 3) Of the accurate choices, keep only the one that demonstrates the point the sentence is making.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: Two or three choices are true readings of the data, but only one proves the passage's point.
You pick an accurate comparison that doesn't show it, for example comparing two places with the same climate when the point is that climates differ.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
Two or three choices are true readings of the data, but only one proves the passage's point.
You pick an accurate comparison that doesn't show it, for example comparing two places with the same climate when the point is that climates differ.
